# PixelHUD

> A Minecraft-style HUD overlay for Mac and Windows. Battery = hearts. Keystrokes = XP. Closed apps = kill feed.

## What is PixelHUD?

PixelHUD is a desktop overlay application that gamifies your computer in real time using Minecraft's iconic HUD aesthetic. It displays a persistent overlay at the bottom of your screen (like a Minecraft game HUD) and animates background elements that react to your real system activity.

## Who is it for?

- Minecraft fans who want their Mac or Windows PC to feel like a game
- Developers and knowledge workers who want a fun, gamified productivity boost
- Anyone who wants to see their battery as hearts instead of a percentage
- Gamers who use their Mac for work and want it to feel like an RPG

## Key Features

- **Battery as hearts**: Battery level is displayed as Minecraft heart containers — low battery = low health
- **XP bar from keystrokes**: Every keystroke fills your XP bar and levels you up
- **Kill feed**: When you close an app, a kill feed notification appears ("Chrome was slain")
- **Walking mobs**: Passive mobs walk across the background of your screen
- **Creeper explosion on Cmd+X**: Cutting text triggers a Creeper explosion animation
- **Achievements**: Unlock achievements for productivity milestones
- **Friends leaderboard**: Compare XP with friends
- **Focus Mode**: Hide distractions for deep work sessions
- **Free**: No payment required

## System Requirements

- macOS 13 (Ventura) or later
- Windows 10 or later

## Download / Access

- Website: https://minecrafthud.eliaspfeffer.de/
- Windows download: https://github.com/eliaspfeffer/MinecraftHUD-releases/releases/latest/download/PixelHUD-Setup.exe

## FAQs

**What is PixelHUD?**
A desktop overlay app that shows your Mac/Windows system stats as Minecraft UI elements — hearts for battery, XP bar for keystrokes, kill feed for closed apps.

**Is PixelHUD free?**
Yes. Both the macOS and Windows versions are free to download.

**Does it work on Apple Silicon (M1/M2/M3/M4)?**
Yes, fully supports Apple Silicon and Intel Macs running macOS 13+.

**Will it slow down my Mac?**
No. It's a lightweight overlay with minimal CPU and memory footprint.

**What does the kill feed show?**
When you quit an application, a message appears in the top-right corner like "Chrome was slain" or "Spotify eliminated", styled like Minecraft's kill feed.
